title: How the overlay got to the goal
lede: Cosmos Reason watched the indexed play, graded every overlay it was shown, and the cut changed because of what it kept marking wrong.

originals.label: First indexed clip
originals.detail: 10 seconds. The five graded rounds used this file. The reasoner describes a dribble, a pass, a shot, and a save. The goal is not in it yet.

originals.label: Clip with the goal
originals.detail: 11 seconds. The same play, plus the second where the ball is in the net. This is the input for the final cut.

reasoning.perceive: A competitive college soccer match between UCLA and Duke with the score tied 1-1 in the second half, featuring dribbling, passing, a shot on goal, and a save by the Duke goalkeeper.

events.caption: A UCLA player in a white jersey dribbles the ball near the center of the field while being closely pursued by a Duke player in a blue jersey.
The UCLA player in white passes the ball to a teammate also in white, who is positioned closer to the Duke goal.
The UCLA teammate takes a shot on goal, but the Duke goalkeeper in yellow makes a save.
A Duke player in blue clears the ball, and the play continues with both teams vying for possession in the midfield.

segments.text: The video shows a soccer match between UCLA and Duke, with the score tied at 1-1 in the second half. A player in a white jersey, number 9, dribbles the ball upfield, evading a defender in a blue jersey. He passes to a teammate in white, number 26, who is positioned near the penalty area. The player in white number 26 takes a shot on goal, but the Duke goalkeeper, dressed in yellow, makes a save. The ball is then cleared by a Duke player in blue, and the play continues with both teams contesting for possession. The camera follows the action as players move across the field, with the scoreboard and game clock visible in the top left corner.

The video shows a soccer match between UCLA and Duke during the NCAA Championship Second Round, with the score tied at 1-1 in the second half. The scene is set on a well-maintained green field with white boundary lines and a goalpost visible in the background. Players from both teams are actively engaged in the game, wearing blue and white uniforms. The clock in the top right corner indicates the remaining time in the second half. The action focuses on a player in a blue uniform who is dribbling the ball near the center of the field, surrounded by opponents in white. As the play develops, the player in blue attempts to maneuver past defenders, but a player in white intercepts the ball and quickly passes it to a teammate. The ball is then crossed into the penalty area, where another player in white takes a shot at the goal. The goalkeeper, dressed in yellow, dives to his left in an attempt to save the shot but fails to stop the ball, which goes into the net. The crowd and stadium environment are not visible...

A player in a blue jersey, number 10, takes a shot from outside the penalty area. The ball travels toward the goal, where the goalkeeper in yellow dives to his left in an attempt to save it. The ball beats the goalkeeper and enters the net, resulting in a goal. The player who scored, number 10, runs forward and celebrates with his arms raised. Other players on the field react to the goal, with some raising their arms in celebration or disappointment. The scoreboard shows UCLA 1, Duke 1, with 2:53 remaining in the second half.

after.title: The box follows the ball
after.because: Round after round, the grade said the disc or the arrow was on a blue Duke shirt while the white player had the ball, and that a label stayed up after the action had moved. This cut stops guessing a role. It draws the ball from the detector frame that measured it, and a circle under the player at the ball.
good: The box is on the ball on the frame it was measured, including when the camera pans.
When the detector does not see the ball, the box is absent instead of sitting on grass.
bad: It is still a diagram. A kick and a shot do not change the picture.

after.title: Hits get a sound and a punch
after.because: The ball track was right and the picture was flat. Kicks, the pass, and the shot now zoom in over time, shake, and carry a hit sound. The shot slows down.
good: The zoom travels in instead of cutting to a cropped frame.
Slow motion is darker than the live picture, so the shot feels different from the run of play.
bad: This file still ends on the save. The goal has not been added to the upload yet.

after.title: The goal cut
after.because: The new upload includes the scoring second. The zoom pushes into the net, the slow motion stays dark, a light opens on the ball in the goal, and the picture holds afterward with confetti and a cheer.

critique.summary: The highlight shows a soccer play where a shot is saved, followed by a goal. The edit includes a zoom into the goal, slow motion, and a celebration with confetti.
good: The zoom into the goal and the slow motion effect are well-timed and enhance the dramatic impact of the goal.
The confetti and celebration after the goal add to the celebratory feel of the highlight.
The use of a light flare on the ball in the net adds a cinematic touch to the goal moment.
bad: The ball box effect is not visible in the frames, which may affect the readability of the ball's position during the play.
The timing of the zoom and slow motion could be slightly adjusted to better align with the exact moment of the goal.

issues.detail: The ball box effect is not visible in the frames, which may affect the readability of the ball's position during the play.
issues.fix: Ensure the ball box effect is visible in the frames to improve readability.

issues.detail: The timing of the zoom and slow motion could be slightly adjusted to better align with the exact moment of the goal.
issues.fix: Adjust the timing of the zoom and slow motion to better align with the exact moment of the goal.
